name: Festus (procurator)
title: Procurator of the Roman Empire in Judea
summary: Porcius Festus was the Roman procurator who succeeded Felix in Judea. He inherited Paul's case from his predecessor and arranged the famous trial where Paul defended himself before King Agrippa II, which ultimately led to Paul being sent to Rome to stand trial before the emperor.

keyEvents.title: Succeeds Felix as procurator
keyEvents.description: Festus took over the office of procurator in Judea after Felix and thus inherited the unresolved case against Paul.

keyEvents.title: The Jews bring charges against Paul
keyEvents.description: Shortly after his arrival, Festus went to Jerusalem, where the Jewish leaders presented their accusations against Paul and asked for him to be transferred there.

keyEvents.title: Paul appeals to Caesar
keyEvents.description: When Festus suggested that Paul should be tried in Jerusalem, Paul used his right as a Roman citizen to appeal directly to the emperor in Rome.

keyEvents.title: Consulting with King Agrippa
keyEvents.description: Festus presented Paul's case to King Agrippa II and his sister Berenice during their visit, as he was unsure what to write to the emperor.

keyEvents.title: Declares that Paul is mad
keyEvents.description: During Paul's defense speech, Festus interrupted him loudly and declared that his extensive learning had driven him mad, which Paul calmly refuted.

keyEvents.title: Acknowledges Paul's innocence
keyEvents.description: After the hearing, Festus and Agrippa concluded that Paul had done nothing deserving of death or imprisonment, but must be sent to Rome since he had appealed.
